original_question: Does every right-orderable n-Engel group admit a Conrad right order?
target_in_paper: Section 2.1, Problem 2.8 (A. H. Rhemtulla): "Does every right-orderable n-Engel group have a Conrad right order?" This is the exact official formulation your draft is aiming at, rather than the broader Problem 2.35 about right-orderable groups without non-abelian free subgroups. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/0906.2621.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft is already extremely close to the paper: it matches both the hypothesis class (right-orderable n-Engel groups) and the conclusion sought (existence of a Conrad right order), and it is almost verbatim Problem 2.8. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/0906.2621.pdf))
missing_details: The paper's quantifier is over a fixed positive integer n; "n-Engel" means the same n works for all x,y in G, unlike a general Engel group, and the notation [x,{}_n y] denotes the iterated commutator of x with n copies of y. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/0906.2621.pdf))
To be fully stand-alone, "right-orderable" should be unpacked as "admits a total order invariant under right multiplication." ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/0906.2621.pdf))
A "Conrad right order" needs its defining inequality: if 1<f<g, then f g^m f^{-1}>g for some positive integer m=m(f,g). ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/0906.2621.pdf))

The conclusion is existential: the group need only admit some Conrad right order; the problem does not ask whether every right order on such a group is Conrad. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/0906.2621.pdf))
The nearby context also records the sharper equivalent form of the Conrad condition used here: m may always be taken to be 2. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/0906.2621.pdf))
refined_question: For each positive integer n, if a group G admits a total order invariant under right multiplication and satisfies the n-Engel identity [x,{}_n y]=1 for all x,y in G, where [x,{}_1 y]=x^{-1}y^{-1}xy and [x,{}_{k+1} y]=[[x,{}_k y],y], must G admit a right-invariant total order < with the Conrad property that whenever 1<f<g, there exists m=m(f,g) in Z_{>0} such that f g^m f^{-1}>g? ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/0906.2621.pdf))
equivalent_formulation: For each positive integer n, does every right-orderable n-Engel group admit a right order < such that 1<f<g implies f g^2 f^{-1}>g for all f,g in G? The paper explicitly notes that in the Conrad condition one may always take m=2. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/0906.2621.pdf))
justification: Section 1 supplies the paper's convention that an n-Engel group has a single fixed n>0 working uniformly for all pairs x,y, in contrast with a general Engel group where n may depend on x and y. The opening paragraph of Section 2 then defines a Conrad right-ordering via the inequality 1<f<g implies f g^m f^{-1}>g for some positive integer m, and Problem 2.8 asks exactly whether every right-orderable n-Engel group has such an order. The nearby comments give the paper-faithful scope: Comment 2.25 records a positive answer when n<=4, while Comment 2.35 notes that no right-orderable group satisfying a group identity was then known to fail Conrad right-orderability. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/0906.2621.pdf))
